facts.text: SNAP-19 RTG Power Booms was deployed at Interstellar Trajectory — Aldebaran & Aquila during Pioneer 10 & 11 in 1972.
facts.source: US Dept of Energy / NASA Ames

facts.text: Twin deployable 3-meter truss booms holding four SNAP-19 radioisotope thermoelectric generators fueled by decaying plutonium-238.
facts.source: US Dept of Energy / NASA Ames

facts.text: Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
Provided continuous electrical power for over three decades in the deep freeze of outer space where solar panels cannot function.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Interstellar Trajectory — Aldebaran & Aquila.
Demonstrated the safety and durability of RTG nuclear power for outer planet exploration.

scenes.kids: I am SNAP-19 RTG Power Booms. I arrived here at Interstellar Trajectory — Aldebaran & Aquila in 1972.
scenes.explorer: SNAP-19 RTG Power Booms, Pioneer 10 & 11: deployed at Interstellar Trajectory — Aldebaran & Aquila in 1972.

scenes.kids: Take a look at how I was built. Every part of me had a special purpose.
scenes.explorer: Twin deployable 3-meter truss booms holding four SNAP-19 radioisotope thermoelectric generators fueled by decaying plutonium-238.

scenes.kids: Out here, there is no air or weather like on Earth, so I had to work smoothly in the cold.
scenes.explorer: Designed to withstand radiation, cosmic dust, and extreme temperature swings without failing.

scenes.kids: My mission finished, but I stay here resting peacefully on the surface.
